p.src: Now Cao Cao, digging where the golden light had appeared, unearthed a bronze bird and asked Xun You, “What omen is this?” Xun You replied, “In ancient times, Emperor Shun’s mother dreamed that a jade bird flew into her bosom, and thereafter gave birth to Shun. Now that you have obtained a bronze bird, this too is an auspicious sign.” Cao Cao was overjoyed and ordered a lofty terrace built to commemorate the event. That very day they broke ground, felled timber, fired tiles, and dressed bricks, beginning construction of the Bronze Bird Terrace above the Zhang River. It was estimated that the work would be completed in a year. Cao Cao’s younger son Cao Zhi came forward and said, “If storied terraces are to be built, there must be three: let the lofty one in the center be named Bronze Bird; let the one on the left be named Jade Dragon; and let the one on the right be named Golden Phoenix. Then build two soaring bridges that span the air and rise between them; it will make a magnificent sight.” Cao Cao said, “My son’s proposal is excellent. When the terraces are completed, they will be enough to delight me in my old age!” Cao Cao had five sons, but Cao Zhi alone was quick-witted and intelligent and excelled at literary composition; Cao Cao had always loved him best.

p.src: Cao Cao therefore left Cao Zhi and Cao Pi in Ye Commandery to oversee construction of the terraces, and ordered Zhang Yan to guard the northern camp. Taking the troops he had acquired from Yuan Shao, five or six hundred thousand in all, Cao Cao led his army back to the capital at Xu and richly rewarded his meritorious officers. He also petitioned that the late Guo Jia be enfeoffed as Marquis Zhen and raised Guo Jia’s son Yi in his own household. He then gathered his many advisers to discuss a southern expedition against Liu Biao. Xun Yu said, “The great army has only just returned from its northern campaign and should not be mobilized again yet. Wait half a year while the men rest and build their strength; then Liu Biao and Sun Quan can both be brought down in a single onslaught.” Cao Cao accepted his advice and divided his troops among agricultural colonies, keeping them ready for deployment.

p.src: Now since Xuande’s arrival in Jingzhou, Liu Biao had treated him with great generosity. One day, as they were drinking together, a sudden report arrived that the surrendered commanders Zhang Wu and Chen Sun were plundering the people in Jiangxia and conspiring together to rebel. Liu Biao exclaimed in alarm, “These two villains have rebelled again; the trouble they cause will not be slight!” Xuande said, “Elder brother, you need not worry. I, Bei, ask leave to go and punish them.” Liu Biao was delighted and immediately mustered thirty thousand troops for Xuande to take with him. Xuande accepted the command and set out at once; before many days had passed, he reached Jiangxia. Zhang Wu and Chen Sun led out their troops to meet him. Xuande rode out beneath the gate banner with Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, and Zhao Yun. He saw from afar that Zhang Wu’s mount was an exceptionally magnificent steed. Xuande said, “That must surely be a thousand-li horse.”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, Zhao Yun leveled his spear, rode out, and charged straight into the enemy formation. Zhang Wu spurred his horse forward to meet him, but in fewer than three bouts Zhao Yun thrust him from the saddle with a single spear stroke, seized the reins at once, and led the horse back to his own lines. Seeing this, Chen Sun chased after him to seize the horse. Zhang Fei gave a mighty shout, charged straight out with his spear, and stabbed Chen Sun to death. The rest all broke and fled. Xuande offered amnesty to the remaining followers, restored order throughout the counties of Jiangxia, and led his army home. Liu Biao came beyond the city walls to welcome him, escorted him into the city, and held a banquet to celebrate his victory. When the wine had begun to take effect, Liu Biao said, “With such heroic talent as yours, my brother, Jingzhou has someone it can rely upon. I worry only that the southern Yue may raid us without warning, while Zhang Lu and Sun Quan are also causes for concern.” Xuande said, “I have three commanders who are fully fit for such assignments: send Zhang Fei to patrol the southern Yue frontier; have Yunchang hold Zicheng securely to contain Zhang Lu; and have Zhao Yun guard Sanjiang to withstand Sun Quan; what is there to fear?”

p.src: Liu Biao was pleased and wished to follow his advice. Cai Mao told his elder sister, Lady Cai, “Liu Bei means to station his three commanders outside while he himself remains in Jingzhou. In time he will surely become a danger.” That night Lady Cai said to Liu Biao, “I hear that many people in Jingzhou associate with Liu Bei. You cannot afford to leave him unguarded against. There is no benefit in allowing him to remain within the city now; it would be better to send him elsewhere.” Liu Biao said, “Xuande is a benevolent man.” Lady Cai replied, “I only fear that others do not share your way of thinking.” Liu Biao pondered in silence and gave no answer.

p.src: The next day, as Liu Biao left the city, he saw that Xuande’s mount was an exceptionally fine horse. On asking about it, he learned that it had belonged to Zhang Wu, and praised it without end. Xuande thereupon presented the horse to Liu Biao. Liu Biao was delighted and rode it back into the city. Kuai Yue saw the horse and asked him about it. Liu Biao said, “Xuande gave it to me.” Kuai Yue said, “My late elder brother Kuai Liang was supremely skilled at judging horses, and I too understand something of the art. This horse has tear grooves beneath its eyes and a white mark beside its forehead. It is known as Dilu, and whoever rides it brings harm upon its master. Zhang Wu died because of this horse. My lord, you must not ride it.”

p.src: Liu Biao heeded his words. The next day he invited Xuande to a banquet and said, “Yesterday you favored me with a fine horse, and I am deeply grateful for your generous kindness. But since you, worthy brother, are often called upon to campaign, you can make good use of it. I respectfully return it to you.” Xuande rose and thanked him. Liu Biao continued, “You have lived here a long while, worthy brother, and I fear your martial affairs may fall into neglect. Xinye County, a dependency of Xiangyang, is fairly well supplied with money and grain. What would you say to taking your own troops and stationing them in that county?”

p.src: Xuande accepted the proposal. The next day he bade farewell to Liu Biao and led his own troops straight to Xinye. Just as he passed through the city gate, a man appeared before his horse, bowed deeply, and said, “My lord, you must not ride that horse.” Xuande looked and saw that it was Yi Ji, styled Jibo, a native of Shanyang and a retainer in the Jingzhou administration. Xuande hurriedly dismounted and asked him what he meant. Yi Ji said, “Yesterday I heard Kuai Yidu tell the Governor of Jingzhou, ‘This horse is called Dilu, and whoever rides it brings harm upon its master.’ That is why it was returned to you. How can you ride it again?” Xuande said, “I am deeply grateful for your concern for me. But every man’s life and death are ordained by fate; how could a horse bring harm upon him?” Yi Ji greatly admired the loftiness of his view and thereafter kept in regular contact with Xuande.

p.src: After Xuande arrived in Xinye, soldiers and commoners alike rejoiced, and the administration was entirely renewed. In the spring of the twelfth year of Jian’an, Lady Gan gave birth to Liu Shan. That night a white crane flew down onto the roof of the county offices, cried loudly more than forty times, and then flew westward. At the moment of the birth, a wondrous fragrance filled the room. Lady Gan had once dreamed at night that she looked upward and swallowed the Northern Dipper; therefore the child was given the infant name Adou.

p.src: At this time Cao Cao was personally leading his troops on a northern campaign. Xuande therefore went to Jingzhou and said to Liu Biao, “Cao Cao is now campaigning in the north, leaving Xuchang undefended. If we use the forces of Jingzhou and Xiangyang to strike it while the opportunity offers, our great enterprise can be accomplished.” Liu Biao replied, “It is enough for me to sit securely in possession of Jingzhou. Why should I seek anything more?” Xuande fell silent. Liu Biao invited him into the rear hall to drink. When the wine had begun to take effect, Liu Biao suddenly heaved a long sigh. Xuande asked, “Elder brother, why do you sigh so deeply?” Liu Biao said, “There is a matter troubling me, but it is not easy to speak of plainly.” Just as Xuande was about to ask again, Lady Cai came out and stood behind the screen. Liu Biao lowered his head and said nothing.

p.src: Presently the banquet ended, and Xuande returned to Xinye. By the winter of that year, Cao Cao was reported to have returned from Liucheng, and Xuande deeply lamented that Liu Biao had not followed his advice. Then one day a messenger arrived from Liu Biao, inviting Xuande to meet him in Jingzhou. Xuande accompanied the messenger there. Liu Biao received him, and after they had exchanged the proper courtesies, invited him into the rear hall for a banquet. He then said, “I have lately heard that Cao Cao has led his army back to the capital at Xu. His power grows stronger by the day, and he surely intends to swallow up Jingzhou and Xiangyang. I regret that I did not heed your advice before and thus lost so fine an opportunity!” Xuande replied, “The realm is divided today, and warfare erupts more with each passing day. How could opportunities ever be exhausted? If you can seize one when it next arises, there is no need for regret.” Liu Biao said, “My brother’s words are entirely sound.” The two then drank together, facing one another.

p.src: When the wine had taken effect, Liu Biao suddenly began to weep. Xuande asked him why. Liu Biao said, “There is a matter weighing on my mind. I wished to confide it to you before, worthy brother, but found no suitable occasion.” Xuande said, “What difficult matter can you not decide, elder brother? If there is any way you can employ me, I will not refuse, even at the cost of my life.” Liu Biao said, “My elder son Qi, born to my first wife, Lady Chen, is a worthy man, but he is too weak and timid to accomplish great affairs; my younger son Cong, born to my present wife, Lady Cai, is quite intelligent. I wish to set aside the elder and establish the younger, but fear that this would violate propriety and law; yet if I establish my elder son, all the members of Lady Cai’s clan command military affairs and will surely cause disorder afterward. Thus I cannot reach a decision.” Xuande said, “From ancient times, setting aside the elder to establish the younger has been the road to disorder. If you fear the power of the Cai clan, you may gradually diminish it; you must not establish your younger son out of doting affection.” Liu Biao fell silent. As it happened, Lady Cai had always been suspicious of Xuande, and whenever he conversed with Liu Biao, she would secretly listen. At that very moment she was behind a screen, and when she heard Xuande’s words, she bitterly resented him.

p.src: Xuande realized that he had spoken amiss, so he rose to go to the privy. Seeing that flesh had grown again on his thighs, he too could not help shedding tears. A short while later, he returned to the banquet. Seeing tears on Xuande’s face, Liu Biao asked in surprise what was wrong. Xuande sighed deeply and said, “In former days, I, Bei, was never out of the saddle, and the flesh of my thighs remained lean; now, having gone so long without riding, flesh has grown on them. The days and months slip idly by; old age is approaching, yet I have achieved nothing. That is why I grieve!” Liu Biao said, “I have heard that when you were in Xuchang, you and Cao Cao warmed wine with green plums and discussed the heroes of the age. You named every famous man then living, but Cao Cao dismissed them all and said only, ‘The heroes of the realm are none but you, my lord, and Cao.’ Even a man of Cao Cao’s power did not dare place himself before you. Why then should you worry that you will achieve nothing?” Carried away by the wine, Xuande let slip, “If I, Bei, only had a firm base, the mediocre men of the realm would truly be no cause for concern.” Hearing this, Liu Biao said nothing. p.src: Seeing Liu Biao hesitate and remain undecided, Cai Mao secretly conferred with Lady Cai. They planned to summon all the officials to a grand gathering in Xiangyang that very day and carry out their scheme there. The next day, Cai Mao reported to Liu Biao, “The harvests have been abundant in recent years. We ought to gather all the officials in Xiangyang to show them our solicitude and goodwill. I ask you, my lord, to attend.” Liu Biao said, “My ailment of the vital breath has flared up recently, and I truly cannot go. Let my two sons preside and receive the guests.” Cai Mao said, “The young lords are still too young; I fear they may fall short in matters of ceremony.” Liu Biao said, “Then go to Xinye and invite Xuande to receive the guests.” Cai Mao secretly rejoiced that this fit his scheme exactly, and at once sent a man to invite Xuande to Xiangyang.

The next day, Cai Mao reported to Liu Biao, “The harvests have been abundant in recent years. We ought to gather all the officials in Xiangyang to show them our solicitude and goodwill.
I ask you, my lord, to attend.”
Liu Biao said, “My ailment of the vital breath has flared up recently, and I truly cannot go.
Let my two sons preside and receive the guests.”
Cai Mao said, “The young lords are still too young; I fear they may fall short in matters of ceremony.”
Liu Biao said, “Then go to Xinye and invite Xuande to receive the guests.”

p.src: Meanwhile, after racing back to Xinye, Xuande knew that his careless words had brought trouble upon him, but he told no one about it. Suddenly a messenger arrived, inviting him to Xiangyang. Sun Qian said, “Yesterday I saw you return in great haste, my lord, and you seemed deeply troubled. By my humble reckoning, something must have happened in Jingzhou. Now that this sudden invitation to a gathering has come, you must not go lightly.” Only then did Xuande relate the preceding events to them all. Yunchang said, “Brother, you merely suspect that you misspoke. Liu of Jingzhou has shown no sign of anger or reproach. The words of outsiders should not be lightly believed. Xiangyang is not far from here. If you do not go, Jingzhou will instead become suspicious.” Xuande said, “Yunchang is right.” Zhang Fei said, “No good feast and no good meeting await you. Better not go.” Zhao Yun said, “I will accompany you with three hundred cavalry and infantry. I can ensure that no harm comes to you, my lord.” Xuande said, “That will be excellent.” So he and Zhao Yun set out for Xiangyang that very day.

p.src: The next day, word came that the officials of the nine commanderies and forty-two districts had all arrived. Cai Mao had already summoned Kuai Yue to consult with him, saying, “Liu Bei is a formidable hero of the age. If he remains here long, he will surely bring harm in the future. I fear it will be difficult to strike.” Cai Mao said, “I have five hundred soldiers lying in ambush within the city, ready for action.” Kuai Yue said, “Have Wen Ping and Wang Wei arrange a separate banquet in the outer hall for the military officers. First detain Zhao Yun there; then the deed can be done.”

p.src: Cai Mao followed his advice. That very day, cattle and horses were slaughtered, and a magnificent banquet was laid out. Xuande rode Dilu to the provincial offices and ordered the horse led into the rear garden and tethered there. All the officials assembled in the hall. Xuande occupied the seat of honor; the two young lords sat one on either side, and the rest took their places according to rank. Zhao Yun stood, sword at his side, beside Xuande. Wen Ping and Wang Wei came in and invited Zhao Yun to join the feast. Zhao Yun declined and would not go. Xuande ordered him to take his seat, so Zhao Yun reluctantly obeyed and went out. He sent all three hundred soldiers Xuande had brought back to their lodgings and waited only until the guests were half drunk before giving the signal to strike.

p.src: After three rounds of wine, Yi Ji rose to offer toasts. When he reached Xuande, he caught his eye and whispered, “Please go and change your clothes.” Xuande understood his meaning and at once rose to visit the privy. When Yi Ji had finished offering the toasts, he hurried into the rear garden, caught up with Xuande, and whispered in his ear, “Cai Mao has devised a plot to kill you. Troops guard all three approaches outside the city—the east, south, and north. Only the west gate offers escape. You must flee at once!” Greatly alarmed, Xuande hurriedly untied Dilu, opened the rear-garden gate, and led the horse out. Leaping into the saddle, he gave no thought to his attendants but galloped alone toward the west gate. The gatekeeper questioned him, but Xuande made no reply and lashed his horse through the gate. The gatekeeper tried but failed to stop him, then hastened to report to Cai Mao. Cai Mao immediately mounted and led five hundred troops in pursuit.

p.src: Now Xuande, having burst through the west gate and ridden many li, found a broad stream ahead blocking his way. This was the Tan Stream, several zhang wide; its waters flowed into the Xiang River, and its current was exceedingly swift. Reaching the bank and seeing that he could not cross, Xuande reined in and turned back. In the distance west of the city, clouds of dust billowed up—the pursuers were almost upon him. Xuande cried, “This time I am done for!” He therefore turned his horse back toward the stream. When he looked back, the pursuing troops were already close. In his panic, Xuande spurred his horse down into the stream. Before they had gone more than a few paces, the horse’s forehooves suddenly sank, and Xuande’s robe was soaked. Xuande lashed the horse and shouted, “Dilu! Dilu! Today you have failed me!” As soon as he had spoken, the horse suddenly surged up from the water and, with a single leap of three zhang, flew onto the western bank.
